ixbrl.demoText:
Our organisation employs 1,247 employees in full-time equivalents as of 31 December 2024, of whom 847 are on open-ended contracts and 400 on fixed-term or temporary contracts. Women account for 48% of our workforce.

In the 2024 financial year, our gross Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions amount to 12,450 tCO₂e and our Scope 2 emissions (location-based) to 3,820 tCO₂e. Total Scope 1+2+3 reaches 87,300 tCO₂e, representing a carbon intensity of 43.6 tCO₂e per million euros of net revenue.

We consume 124,500 MWh of energy in total, of which 68% from renewable sources (84,660 MWh) and 32% from fossil sources (39,840 MWh). Energy intensity stands at 62.2 MWh per million euros of revenue.

gs1.title: Create your account and set up your organization
gs1.content:
## Create your account

1. Go to the sign-up page and enter your professional email.
2. Choose a password (min. 8 characters, 1 uppercase, 1 digit).
3. Verify your email and click the confirmation link.

## Set up your organization

On first access, the onboarding wizard guides you through 4 steps:
- **Industry** — NAF / NACE code for sector benchmarking.
- **Headcount** — determines applicable CSRD thresholds.
- **Geographic scope** — for regional indicators.
- **Standards** — select target frameworks (CSRD, GRI, TCFD…).

> **Tip**: you can change these settings at any time in **Settings › Organization**.

gs2.title: Import your first ESG data
gs2.content:
## Accepted formats

- **CSV / Excel** (xlsx, xls) — columns: indicator, value, unit, period, source.
- **REST API** — endpoint `POST /api/v1/indicators/bulk`.
- **Native connectors** — SAP, Sage, Oracle (Pro+ plan).

## CSV import procedure

1. Download the **CSV template** from *Data › Import*.
2. Fill in your data respecting the columns.
3. Drag the file into the drop zone.
4. Review the preview and fix any flagged errors.
5. Click **Validate import**.

Common errors: wrong decimal separator (use period `.`), dates not in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD), unrecognized units (check the units library).

gs3.title: Understanding your ESG dashboard
gs3.content:
## Executive dashboard anatomy

The dashboard has three zones:

1. **Overall score /100** — weighted aggregate of E, S, G pillars.
2. **Trends** — 12-month evolution, compared to sector.
3. **AI alerts** — anomalies and priority recommendations.

## Understanding your score

| Range | Level | Meaning |
|-------|-------|----------|
| 80–100 | Leader | Exemplary ESG performance |
| 60–79 | Advanced | Good trajectory, some areas for improvement |
| 40–59 | Progressing | Corrective actions to initiate |
| < 40 | Beginner | Progress plan recommended |

## Customize weights

Go to **Settings › Methodology** to adjust E/S/G pillar weighting according to your strategy.

c1.title: Difference between Scope 1, 2 and 3
c1.content:
## The three emission scopes

**Scope 1 — Direct emissions**: combustion in your own facilities and vehicles.

**Scope 2 — Indirect energy emissions**: purchased electricity, steam, heat.

**Scope 3 — Other indirect emissions** (15 GHG Protocol categories):
- *Upstream*: purchased goods & services, capital goods, business travel…
- *Downstream*: use of sold products, end-of-life, franchises…

> **CSRD note**: the directive requires disclosure of Scopes 1, 2 and relevant Scope 3 categories.

## Built-in emission factors

ESG Flow includes the ADEME database (France) and IEA factors for 80+ countries. They are updated automatically every quarter.

c2.title: Set up your SBTi decarbonization plan
c2.content:
## What is SBTi?

The *Science Based Targets* initiative (SBTi) allows companies to set emission reduction targets aligned with a +1.5°C or +2°C trajectory.

## In ESG Flow

1. Go to **Decarbonization › SBTi Plan**.
2. Set your **baseline year** and **target horizon** (2030, 2050).
3. The tool automatically calculates the required annual trajectory.
4. Add your **actions** (energy efficiency, green procurement, mobility…) with their estimated impact.
5. Track progress in real time on the convergence chart.

r1.title: Generate your CSRD / ESRS report
r1.content:
## CSRD overview

The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) applies progressively from 2024. It requires publishing sustainability information according to ESRS standards.

## In ESG Flow — CSRD Report Builder

1. Go to **Reports › CSRD Builder**.
2. Select your **applicable ESRS** (auto-detected based on your sector and size).
3. Previously entered data is **pre-filled** automatically.
4. Complete missing fields (flagged in orange).
5. Click **Generate report** — Word, PDF or iXBRL/ESEF (XHTML EFRAG) format.

## Detailed audit trail

Each data point carries a UTC timestamp and SHA-256 fingerprint, with source → calculation → report traceability to facilitate your external auditor's work.

r2.title: Schedule automatic reports
r2.content:
## Scheduled reports

In **Reports › Scheduled Reports**, configure:

- **Frequency**: monthly, quarterly, annual.
- **Format**: PDF, Excel, Word.
- **Recipients**: add stakeholder emails.
- **Framework**: CSRD, GRI, TCFD, PRI or custom.

Reports are generated overnight (00:00 UTC) and sent by email with a secure download link valid for 30 days.

sc1.title: Send questionnaires to your suppliers
sc1.content:
## Supply Chain module

ESG Flow lets you evaluate your suppliers across 6 ESG dimensions: environment, labor rights, ethics, diversity, governance, supply chain.

## Send a questionnaire

1. Go to **Supply Chain › Suppliers**.
2. Add your suppliers (CSV import or manual entry).
3. Select the questionnaire **template** (CSRD Tier 1, Duty of Vigilance, custom).
4. Click **Send** — the supplier receives a unique secure link.
5. Track responses and scores in the Supply Chain dashboard.

## Vigilance plan

In accordance with law 2017-399 (Duty of Vigilance), the module automatically generates the vigilance plan with identified corrective actions.

sec1.title: Enable two-factor authentication (2FA)
sec1.content:
## Why enable 2FA?

2FA adds a security layer by requiring, in addition to your password, a 6-digit code generated by an app on your smartphone.

## Compatible apps

Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Bitwarden.

## Setup

1. Go to **Settings › Security**.
2. Click **Enable 2FA**.
3. Scan the QR code with your app.
4. Enter the displayed 6-digit code to confirm.
5. **Save your 8 backup codes** in a safe place (password manager).

> If you lose your phone, use a backup code to log in.

sec2.title: Manage user roles and permissions
sec2.content:
## Available roles

| Role | Rights |
|------|--------|
| **Admin** | Full access, user management and billing |
| **Manager** | Read + write on all data, no billing access |
| **Contributor** | Data entry and modification within their scope only |
| **Viewer** | Read-only, export allowed |

## Invite a user

1. Go to **Settings › Users**.
2. Click **Invite**.
3. Enter the email and desired role.
4. The user receives an invitation email valid for 7 days.

api1.title: API Authentication — Bearer Token
api1.content:
## Get your API key

1. Go to **Settings › Integrations › API**.
2. Click **Generate a new key**.
3. Copy the key — it will only be shown once.

## Usage

```http
GET /api/v1/indicators
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
Content-Type: application/json
```

## Quotas & limits

| Plan | Calls / month | Users | Organizations |
|------|--------------|-------|---------------|
| Free | 1,000 | 3 | 5 |
| Starter | 10,000 | 10 | 25 |
| Pro | 100,000 | 50 | 100 |
| Enterprise | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |

api2.title: Configure a webhook
api2.content:
## What are webhooks for?

Webhooks allow ESG Flow to notify your system in real time when events occur: new score calculated, report generated, alert triggered, etc.

## Setup

1. Go to **Settings › Webhooks**.
2. Click **Add an endpoint**.
3. Enter your HTTPS URL (required).
4. Select the events to listen for.
5. Save — a signing secret is generated.

## Signature verification

Each call includes the header `X-ESGFlow-Signature: sha256=<hmac>`. Verify it server-side to secure your endpoint.

context.title: What changed with Omnibus I (December 2025)
context.body: The European Commission adopted the Omnibus Simplification Package I in December 2025. This text substantially amends the CSRD directive (2022/2464/EU) by narrowing its scope, easing reporting requirements and postponing the entry-into-force timelines for waves 2 and 3.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions about the CSRD Omnibus

0.q: My 300-employee company was in wave 2 — is it exempt?
0.a: Yes. With Omnibus I, the threshold rose to 1,000 employees AND €450M revenue. A 300-employee company is no longer directly subject to the CSRD, unless it is listed on a European regulated market. However, it remains exposed to supply-chain pressure from its clients.

1.q: Are the DPEF obligations (article L.225-102-1) maintained?
1.a: The DPEF (Extra-Financial Performance Statement), applicable since 2017 to companies with more than 500 employees, is being progressively replaced by the CSRD. For companies that exceed the new CSRD thresholds, the CSRD replaces the DPEF. For companies below the CSRD thresholds but above the DPEF thresholds (500 emp. or €100M revenue), the DPEF remains applicable until simplification texts are adopted.

2.q: What is the VSME and who does it apply to?
2.a: The VSME (Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for SMEs) is a standard being developed by EFRAG, designed for unlisted SMEs. It is voluntary and streamlined compared to the full ESRS. Its adoption is strongly recommended for SMEs that answer questionnaires from clients or investors. ESG Flow is designed to be compatible with the VSME as soon as it is finalized.

3.q: Have the deadlines for companies already in wave 1 changed?
3.a: No. Companies already subject to the CSRD (large listed companies, former NFRD) keep their initial timelines. Omnibus I only postponed waves 2 and 3 and raised the threshold. The extended wave 1 (>1,000 emp. + €450M revenue) starts for FY 2026.

4.q: Is the EU Taxonomy also streamlined by the Omnibus?
4.a: Omnibus I also contains simplifications for EU Taxonomy reporting (Regulation 2020/852), notably by reducing the quantitative reporting obligations for certain activities. Companies subject to the Taxonomy should consult the amended texts for their specific scope. ESG Flow updates its Taxonomy modules in real time according to the official texts.

intro.heading: What is the EU Taxonomy?
intro.body: The EU Taxonomy (Regulation 2020/852/EU) is a classification system that defines what counts as an environmentally sustainable economic activity. It is the foundation of the European Green Deal, sustainable finance and the reporting obligations of Article 8 of the CSRD.
intro.warningTitle: Only objectives 1 and 2 are operational at this stage
intro.warningBody: Only objectives 1 (mitigation) and 2 (adaptation) have detailed, enforceable technical criteria. Objectives 3 to 6 received their first delegated acts in 2023, but their criteria remain less comprehensive. ESG Flow integrates them progressively as the official texts are published.

objectives.2: Sustainable use of water and marine resources

eligibility.heading: Eligibility vs Alignment: the most common confusion
eligibility.intro: This is the most important distinction — and the one most frequently misunderstood by companies in their first Taxonomy report.

elig.title: Eligibility
elig.defText: Your activity appears in the annexes of the EU Taxonomy (it CAN potentially be "green").
elig.testText: Does my activity appear in the list of activities with technical criteria?
elig.repText: You report the % of eligible revenue/CapEx/OpEx.
elig.warning: Is NOT enough to call yourself "green".

align.title: Alignment
align.defText: Your activity actually meets the 3 cumulative conditions: (1) SC + (2) DNSH + (3) MinSafeguards.
align.testText: Does it contribute substantially + do no significant harm + respect minimum social safeguards?
align.exText: The constructed building must achieve EPC class A energy performance + no water/biodiversity harm + labour rights respected.
align.repText: You report separately the % of aligned revenue/CapEx/OpEx.

0.title: Substantial Contribution (SC)
0.desc: The activity contributes substantially to at least one of the 6 environmental objectives. Precise quantitative thresholds apply — for example, energy performance ≤ local 10th percentile for new buildings (EPC criterion).

1.title: DNSH (Do No Significant Harm)
1.desc: The activity does no significant harm to any of the 5 other environmental objectives. Each objective must be verified individually with specific criteria. Even a 'green' activity such as solar photovoltaic must pass the DNSH water and biodiversity tests.

2.title: Minimum Safeguards (MinSafeguards)
2.desc: Compliance with the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the ILO fundamental conventions and the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.

0.title: Confusing eligibility and alignment
0.desc: Report your % of eligibility AND alignment separately. Saying "X% of our revenue is Taxonomy-compliant" without specifying eligibility vs alignment is a communication error — and a potential regulatory non-compliance.

1.title: Ignoring DNSH for "green" activities
1.desc: A solar energy activity must still pass DNSH water (no impact on water resources), biodiversity (no installation on protected areas), etc. It is not automatic — each objective must be documented.

2.title: Forgetting the Minimum Safeguards
2.desc: Even a perfectly SC + DNSH activity is not aligned if the company does not respect human rights, workers' rights and anti-corruption principles. The G pillar of ESG is necessary for Taxonomy alignment.

3.title: Miscalculating the KPIs (revenue, CapEx, OpEx)
3.desc: Delegated Regulation 2021/2178/EU sets out precise rules for calculating the 3 KPIs. A consulting firm, for example, must carefully distinguish "Taxonomy-eligible" revenue of its services according to the nature of the services actually provided.

4.title: Not documenting the evidence
4.desc: Alignment must be justified by concrete evidence (certifications, energy assessments, supplier attestations, contracts). Without a documentary trail, the auditor will reject the alignment. ESG Flow links each Taxonomy declaration to its supporting documents.

pitfalls.heading: The 5 most common pitfalls
pitfalls.intro: These mistakes recur systematically in first Taxonomy reports. They can lead to restatements, penalties or greenwashing accusations.

0.a: No direct obligation for unlisted SMEs below the post-Omnibus CSRD thresholds. But your large-group clients may ask for your Taxonomy data to calculate their own KPIs. Preparing voluntarily is recommended — and makes it easier to be referenced as a supplier.

1.q: Does the Taxonomy cover social and governance?
1.a: No, the current EU Taxonomy covers only the 6 environmental objectives. The social Taxonomy project is being developed by the Commission, but does not yet have the force of law. Note: the Minimum Safeguards (MinSafeguards) do include a social dimension, but they condition environmental alignment rather than constituting an independent social component.

2.a: Transitional activities (e.g. natural gas vehicles) contribute to decarbonization but without a zero-carbon solution available today. Enabling activities (e.g. wind turbine manufacturing, thermal insulation) allow other activities to achieve the environmental objectives. Both can be aligned with specific technical criteria defined in the annexes of the Taxonomy.

3.a: The Water (3), Circular economy (4), Pollution (5) and Biodiversity (6) objectives received their first delegated acts in 2023. They are applicable but still less detailed compared to objectives 1 and 2, whose criteria cover the vast majority of sectors. ESG Flow integrates them as the official technical texts are published.

intro.title: In 30 seconds
intro.item1: The carbon footprint measures an organisation's greenhouse-gas emissions in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent (tCO₂e).
intro.item2: Global standard methodology: GHG Protocol — 3 scopes (1 = direct, 2 = purchased energy, 3 = value chain).
intro.item3: In France, the BEGES is mandatory for companies with more than 500 employees (Article L229-25).
intro.item4: Under CSRD, the carbon footprint (ESRS E1) is mandatory for the waves concerned, with limited assurance.
intro.item5: Scope 3 represents ~70% of emissions for a B2B services company. Ignoring it means missing the essentials.
intro.item6: The spend-based method (multiplying FEC purchases by ADEME factors) = a pragmatic approach to get started.

definitions.title: What is a carbon footprint?
definitions.p1: A carbon footprint is an inventory of the greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions generated by an organisation over a given scope and period, expressed in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent (tCO₂e).
definitions.p2: CO₂ equivalent makes it possible to aggregate the 7 GHGs of the Kyoto Protocol (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFC, PFC, SF₆, NF₃) into a common unit by multiplying each GHG by its Global Warming Potential (GWP) over 100 years. Methane (CH₄), for example, has a GWP of 28 — 1 tonne of CH₄ equals 28 tCO₂e.
definitions.vocab1: BEGES: Greenhouse-Gas Emissions Assessment — French obligation L229-25
definitions.vocab2: Bilan Carbone®: ADEME method (registered trademark), equivalent to the GHG Protocol
definitions.vocab3: GHG Protocol: international standard (World Resources Institute), the most widely used in the world
definitions.vocab4: ISO 14064: ISO standard for GHG quantification and reporting
definitions.vocab5: BCF (Bilan Carbone Form.®): simplified version run by the APCC

obligations.title: Am I required to do a carbon footprint?
obligations.sanctionBody: Administrative fine of up to €10,000 (€50,000 for repeat offences). Law of 17 August 2015 and its implementing decree — applied since 2019 to ~15 companies/year publicly.
obligations.indirectIntro: Even without a legal obligation, your company is probably required by its customers:
obligations.indirect1: Public procurement: ~40% of French public tenders include an ESG/carbon criterion weighted at least 10%
obligations.indirect2: Large-group customers who must themselves report their Scope 3 — you are one of their category 1 or 4
obligations.indirect3: CSDDD (due-diligence directive, taking effect 2027-2029): supply-chain audits including emissions
obligations.indirect4: Banks & insurers applying the EU Taxonomy and SFDR to their investment portfolios

methodologie.title: The GHG Protocol methodology
methodologie.intro: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004, revised 2015) is the most widely used international standard. It is the basis for almost all other methodologies (ADEME Bilan Carbone, ISO 14064, CDP, SBTi, CSRD ESRS E1).
methodologie.step1: Define the organisational boundary: choice between operational-control, financial-control, or equity-share approaches. Determines which subsidiaries / sites are included.
methodologie.step2: Define the operational boundary: choice of scopes to include (1 mandatory, 2 mandatory, 3 strongly recommended)
methodologie.step3: Identify emission sources by scope: exhaustive list of activities generating GHGs (combustion, electricity, travel, purchases, waste, …)
methodologie.step4: Collect activity data: kWh, litres, km, kg, € depending on the source. This is the most time-consuming step (60-70% of total time).
methodologie.step5: Multiply by emission factors to convert into tCO₂e. Sources: ADEME Base Carbone®, ecoinvent, Climatiq, DEFRA UK, EPA US.

scope1.title: Scope 1: direct emissions
scope1.intro: The Scope 1 covers GHG emissions directly arising from the company's activities — i.e. emitted by sources it controls.
scope1.subTitle: 4 sub-categories

cat0.ex: Boiler 80 kW × 1,800 h = 144,000 kWh gas → 32 tCO₂e (ADEME factor: 0.220 kgCO₂e/kWh NCV)

scope2.title: Scope 2: purchased energy
scope2.intro: The Scope 2 covers indirect emissions linked to energy consumed but produced elsewhere: electricity, steam, heat or cooling purchased from a supplier.
scope2.locationDesc: Average emission factor of the national electricity mix where consumption takes place.
scope2.locationNote: France 2024: 0.0571 kgCO₂e/kWh (very low thanks to nuclear). Germany: 0.338 kgCO₂e/kWh.
scope2.marketDesc: A contractual emission factor: if you have signed a renewable-origin contract, you can count 0 kgCO₂e.
scope2.marketNote: Requires proof: Guarantee of Origin (GO) or CPPA (Corporate Power Purchase Agreement).
scope2.outro: CSRD requires both methods reported separately (ESRS E1-6 §44). BEGES only requires the location-based method.

scope3.title: Scope 3: value chain
scope3.intro: The Scope 3 covers all other indirect emissions in the company's value chain — upstream (purchases, transport, waste) and downstream (use, end-of-life of products sold). The GHG Protocol defines 15 categories.

cat3.name: Energy excl. S1/S2
cat3.desc: Grid losses, extraction of fossil fuels

cat11.name: Use of products
cat11.desc: Energy consumed by the product sold during its life

cat12.name: End-of-life of products
cat12.desc: Sorting, recycling, incineration of products sold

cat13.name: Downstream leased assets
cat13.desc: If you lease out your products (e.g. machines)

scope3.hotNote: 🔥 = categories usually the highest emitters for a French B2B SME.
scope3.methodsTitle: 3 calculation methods (from least to most accurate)

method1.title: 1. Spend-based
method1.desc: Multiply purchase amounts in € by a monetary emission factor (kgCO₂e/€).
method1.note: ✅ Fast: from your accounting FEC. ❌ Average accuracy: ±30%.

method2.title: 2. Average-data
method2.desc: Physical quantities (kg, m³, kWh) × average sector emission factors.
method2.note: ✅ Better accuracy: ±15%. ❌ Requires knowing physical volumes.

method3.title: 3. Supplier-specific
method3.desc: An emission factor provided by each supplier (from their own assessment).
method3.note: ✅ Maximum accuracy (±5%). ❌ Requires obtaining each supplier's assessment — unrealistic for a large portfolio.

scope3.recoBody: For a first assessment, start spend-based on categories 1, 4, 6, 9 (which typically cover 70-90% of Scope 3). Then refine with average-data or supplier-specific on the 3-5 largest items. No need to aim for perfection in the first exercise — a complete assessment with a margin of error is better than no assessment at all.

facteurs.title: ADEME Base Carbone® emission factors
facteurs.intro: ADEME's Base Carbone® is the official French repository — it is the source to use first for an assessment in France. It contains ~5,000 emission factors, updated annually (latest version 2024.4).

exemple.title: Worked example: 80-employee services SME
exemple.intro: Practical case of a French B2B consulting SME, 80 employees, €12M revenue, based in Île-de-France:
exemple.reading1: Total: 2,289 tCO₂e — i.e. 28.6 tCO₂e/employee, in the B2B services sector average (25-40 tCO₂e/empl.)
exemple.reading2: Scope 3 represents 99.4% of the footprint (2,231 tCO₂e). Ignoring it would mean missing the essentials.
exemple.reading3: Scope 3 category 1 (purchases) = 84% of the total. The priority lever is supplier engagement.
exemple.reading4: Scopes 1+2 (58 tCO₂e) represent only 2.5% — but are the fastest to reduce (boiler, car, green electricity contract).

reduction.title: Reduction & SBTi trajectory
reduction.intro: Measuring is not enough — you have to reduce. The SBTi (Science-Based Targets initiative) methodology is the global benchmark for setting reduction targets aligned with the Paris Agreement (limiting warming to 1.5°C).
reduction.commit1: 1.5°C trajectory: -42% of Scope 1+2 emissions by 2030 (vs base year)
reduction.commit2: Net-zero 2050 commitment: -90% of absolute emissions + neutralisation of the residual via carbon capture
reduction.commit3: Scope 3 commitment: -25% of Scope 3 emissions by 2030 (often per category)
reduction.lever1: Energy efficiency: insulation, LED, BMS, sufficiency — generally -10 to -25% on Scopes 1+2 within 2-3 years
reduction.lever2: Electrification: replace fossil combustion with electricity (boiler → heat pump, diesel → EV)
reduction.lever3: Renewable electricity contract: brings Scope 2 market-based to ~0. Caution: not a real physical reduction but a legitimate accounting one.
reduction.lever4: Scope 3 supplier engagement: require a carbon footprint, set contractual targets, switch to low-carbon suppliers
reduction.lever5: Sufficiency: reduce volumes (less flying, more video, remote work, transport pooling)

intro.heading: In 30 seconds
intro.item0: The CSDDD (Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, EU 2024/1760) requires large companies to exercise a due diligence duty across their entire value chain — human rights AND the environment.
intro.item1: Wave 1 applicable on 26 July 2027 (5,000+ employees or €1.5bn revenue), then 2028 and 2029.
intro.item2: Penalties: fines up to 5% of global revenue + expanded civil liability + public naming and shaming.
intro.item3: The trickle-down effect: the large groups concerned will audit their SME/mid-cap suppliers via standardized questionnaires (EcoVadis, Sedex, VendorESG type).
intro.item4: Strong link with ESRS S2 (CSRD): 'Value-chain workers' — same data, dual use.
intro.item5: The French 2017 due diligence law remains applicable until full CSDDD transposition (~2027).

definition.heading: What is the CSDDD?
definition.p1: The Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD or CS3D) is a European directive adopted on 13 June 2024 and published in the OJEU on 5 July 2024 under reference 2024/1760. It requires large EU companies (and certain non-EU companies active in the EU) to exercise a positive obligation to prevent, identify, mitigate, bring to an end and remedy negative impacts on human rights and the environment in their chains of activities (own operations + upstream + limited downstream).
definition.boxItem1: CSDDD = obligation to act on identified impacts (due diligence)
definition.boxFooter: The two directives are complementary and feed each other: what you publish under CSRD ESRS S2 must reflect what you do under CSDDD.

periodes.heading: Application timeline
periodes.intro: The CSDDD enters into application progressively over 3 years, according to company size:
periodes.note: Note: the transposition of the CSDDD into French law must take place before 26 July 2026. The French 2017 due diligence law will be amended or replaced on that occasion.

qui.heading: Who is concerned?
qui.directIntro: All EU companies that, over 2 consecutive financial years, exceed cumulatively:
qui.directItem0: The annual average employee threshold (1,000+ in the final wave)
qui.directItem1: The net global revenue threshold (€450M+ in the final wave)
qui.directFooter: Plus non-EU companies generating > €450M revenue in the EU.
qui.indirectHeading: Indirectly (~several hundred thousand EU companies — including your SME)
qui.dominoTitle: ⚠ The domino effect that concerns you
qui.dominoBody: Companies concerned must identify and audit their direct AND indirect business partners. In concrete terms, if you supply Carrefour, Total, EDF, Orange, Decathlon or Bouygues, they will send you a CSDDD audit questionnaire from 2027 — and make contract renewal conditional on your compliance.

0.t: Integrate due diligence into policies and risk-management systems
0.d: Public policy, dedicated resources, steering committee, annual update.

1.t: Identify and assess actual and potential negative impacts
1.d: Country × sector risk mapping, prioritization by severity × probability.

2.t: Prevent, mitigate or bring identified impacts to an end
2.d: Action plan with deadlines, contractual requirements for suppliers, investment, withdrawal if necessary.

3.d: Accessible to workers, unions, affected communities, whistleblowers. Anonymous and multilingual.

4.d: Quantifiable indicators, internal/external audits, updating of action plans.

5.d: CSDDD report annexed to or integrated into the CSRD ESRS S2 report.

obligations.heading: The 6 key obligations
obligations.intro: Under the CSDDD, the company concerned must implement and demonstrate 6 structuring obligations (art. 5 to 16):

ruissellement.heading: The effect on SMEs: what you will be asked
ruissellement.intro: Even if you are not directly concerned, your large-account clients will send you their CSDDD questionnaire. Here's what to expect:

0.ex: Do you have a public human-rights policy? A signed supplier code of conduct?

1.ex: Who is responsible for due diligence in your organization? What budget is allocated?

2.ex: Have you identified at-risk countries/sectors among YOUR suppliers?

3.ex: What % of your suppliers (by purchase value) were audited this year?

4.ex: Have you had any declared human-rights / environment incidents? How were they resolved?

5.ex: Do you have an anonymous and multilingual channel?

6.ex: % of employees trained in due diligence this year.

7.ex: B Corp, EcoVadis, SA8000, FSC, BSCI, Sedex SMETA, ISO 26000?

ruissellement.oppBody: SMEs that respond quickly and well to these questionnaires become preferred suppliers. Conversely, those that struggle to respond are gradually delisted. The CSDDD is therefore as much an acquisition lever as a constraint.

sanctions.heading: Penalties and civil liability
sanctions.adminItem0: Fine up to 5% of consolidated net global revenue (art. 27)
sanctions.adminItem1: Publication of the decision and the company's name ("naming and shaming")
sanctions.adminItem2: Decision by a designated national supervisory authority (in France: DGCCRF + ACPR expected)
sanctions.civilP1: This is the major legal novelty: the victims of the harm (wronged workers, affected communities, mandated NGOs) can take legal action directly against the French company, even when the harm occurred at a third-party supplier abroad.
sanctions.civilItem0: Minimum limitation period: 5 years (instead of the usual 2-3 years)
sanctions.civilItem1: Eased burden of proof for claimants
sanctions.civilItem2: Possibility of collective action via unions and NGOs
sanctions.civilFooter: In concrete terms: a worker exploited at an Indian subcontractor of a large French group will be able to sue it before the French labour court (Prud'hommes) or commercial court.

methode.heading: 7-step method to prepare
methode.step0: Map your suppliers by risk category (country × sector × purchase amount)
methode.step1: Adopt a supplier code of conduct aligned with the ILO + UN Principles + ESRS S2, contractually signed
methode.step2: Audit critical suppliers (~20% of the portfolio covering 80% of the risk, Pareto principle)
methode.step3: Set up a complaints mechanism accessible to suppliers' employees (phone, web, multilingual)
methode.step4: Formalize an action plan for each non-compliance with deadlines and an owner
methode.step5: Train buyers and sales staff in human-rights/environment assessment criteria
methode.step6: Publish an annual due diligence report (integrated into the CSRD ESRS S2 report if applicable)

0.a: Directly, no — the CSDDD applies only to companies with >1,000 employees and >€450M revenue. Indirectly, yes if you are a supplier to a large group concerned: they will audit you.

1.q: What is the difference between the CSDDD and the French due diligence law?
1.a: The French 2017 law targets ~250 FR companies. The CSDDD extends to ~6,000 EU companies with a harmonized framework, stronger penalties (5% of global revenue) and expanded civil liability. The two coexist until the end of 2027.

2.q: What is the CSDDD application timeline?
2.a: Wave 1 (5,000+ empl., €1.5bn revenue): 26 July 2027. Wave 2 (3,000+ empl., €900M): 26 July 2028. Wave 3 (1,000+ empl., €450M): 26 July 2029.

3.a: Fines up to 5% of net global revenue. Mandatory public naming and shaming. Expanded civil liability: victims can act directly against the French company even for harm abroad.

4.q: How does ESG Flow help with compliance?
4.a: Supply Chain ESG module included from the mid-cap plan: supplier mapping, audit questionnaires, action-plan tracking, complaints register. Compliant with ESRS S2 and CSDDD.

5.q: Does the CSDDD replace the French 2017 law?
5.a: It will replace it after full transposition (~July 2026 in theory). In practice, the 2 regimes coexist and you must comply with the more demanding of the two during the transition period.

6.q: What documents should I prepare to answer a client CSDDD questionnaire?
6.a: Signed supplier code of conduct, human-rights policy, risk mapping, recent audit results, complaints mechanism, corrective action plan. ESG Flow provides templates for all these documents.

scope3.title: What is Scope 3?
scope3.intro: Scope 3 covers all indirect greenhouse gas emissions generated upstream and downstream of a company's activity — that is, excluding its own energy (Scope 1) and purchased electricity (Scope 2). The GHG Protocol breaks Scope 3 down into 15 categories covering the entire value chain.

card1.label: Scope 1

card3.label: Scope 3
card3.desc: 15 upstream + downstream categories — represents 70–90% of the total footprint

scope3.briefTitle: The 15 GHG Protocol categories at a glance
scope3.briefIntro: The GHG Protocol distinguishes upstream categories (linked to purchases and inputs) and downstream categories (linked to sold products and their end of life). Among the most significant:
scope3.brief1: Cat. 1 — Purchased goods & services: purchases from suppliers (often the largest item).
scope3.brief2: Cat. 3 — Energy-related activities: fuel extraction and transport, grid losses.
scope3.brief3: Cat. 4 — Upstream transport: shipping of purchased goods to your sites.
scope3.brief4: Cat. 5 — Waste generated: treatment of waste produced by your operations.
scope3.brief5: Cat. 6 — Business travel: flights, trains, hotels for your employees.
scope3.brief6: Cat. 7 — Employee commuting: employee mobility outside business trips.
scope3.brief7: Cat. 11 — Use of sold products: emissions during end use by your customers.
scope3.brief8: Cat. 12 — End-of-life of sold products: treatment, recycling or incineration after use.
scope3.calloutTitle: Scope 3: mandatory for CSRD, SBTi, CDP
scope3.calloutBody: Scope 3 is required by ESRS E1 (CSRD), by SBTi to validate 1.5°C reduction targets, and by CDP for the Climate questionnaire. It typically represents 70 to 90% of a company's total carbon footprint — ignoring it completely distorts the analysis.

intro.body: If you run or advise a French SME or mid-cap, you have probably heard about the CSRD (Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive) in recent months. Perhaps your statutory auditor warned you, or a major client asked for your ESG report. comprendre.title: Understanding the CSRD in 5 minutes
comprendre.whatP1: The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD, EU Directive 2022/2464) came into force on 5 January 2023. It replaces the NFRD (Non-Financial Reporting Directive) and considerably broadens the scope of companies required to publish a non-financial report.
comprendre.whatP2: Whereas the NFRD covered only ~11,700 large European companies, the CSRD ultimately targets ~50,000 companies — roughly 4× more. In France, an estimated 9,500 companies are directly concerned by the main wave (2024-2026), and several tens of thousands indirectly through pressure from their customers.

row1.scope: Large companies already subject to the NFRD (listed, >500 employees)

row2.scope: All large companies (250+ emp., €40M+ revenue, €20M+ balance sheet)

row4.scope: Non-EU companies with significant EU activity

comprendre.omniIntro: In February 2025, the European Commission proposed a package of simplification measures, known as the “Omnibus”. The key points for SMEs:
comprendre.omni1: Raised threshold: wave 2 now only covers companies with 1,000+ employees (instead of 250) AND €450M+ revenue (instead of €40M)
comprendre.omni2: 2-year postponement: for waves 2 and 3, pushed back to 2027 and 2028
comprendre.omni3: Sector-specific standards dropped: the sector ESRS planned for 2026 are cancelled
comprendre.omni4: Lighter audit: limited assurance maintained, the move toward reasonable assurance abandoned

omniBox.label: 📌 Implication for SMEs
omniBox.body: Many SMEs are <1>no longer directly required to comply with the CSRD post-Omnibus. BUT large groups remain subject to it AND must report ESRS S2 (value chain), which pushes them to demand ESG data from their SME/mid-cap suppliers. The “voluntary” reporting market is therefore booming in parallel. <5>Read our full Omnibus guide →

concernes.title: Am I concerned?
concernes.thresholdIntro: A company is concerned if it exceeds 2 of the 3 thresholds below over 2 consecutive financial years:
concernes.specialTitle: Special cases: you are concerned even below the thresholds
concernes.special1: Listed SME on a European regulated market → wave 3 (2027 publication)
concernes.special2: Subsidiary of a listed group → consolidated into the group's report
concernes.special3: Credit institution or insurer → obligation regardless of size
concernes.special4: Non-EU company with ≥€150M EU revenue + an EU subsidiary or branch → wave 4
concernes.trickleTitle: The trickle-down effect (the “real” issue for SMEs)
concernes.trickleIntro: Even if you exceed no threshold, your large-account customers will ask you for your ESG data. Why?
concernes.trickle1: They have to report their Scope 3 (value-chain emissions, i.e. ~70% of their total emissions for a typical B2B service)
concernes.trickle2: ESRS S2 (“value-chain workers”) requires supplier social audits
concernes.trickle3: The CSDDD directive (duty of vigilance) comes into force gradually 2027-2029 and requires human-rights + environmental risk assessments of suppliers
concernes.trickle4: Public tenders increasingly require ESG criteria (CSR = a weighted criterion ≥10% in ~40% of French public tenders in 2025)
concernes.trickleOutro: Bottom line: if you are an 80-employee SME supplying Total, EDF, Carrefour, Decathlon, Orano or any large listed group, expect to receive within 12 months an ESG questionnaire such as “VendorESG”, “EcoVadis” or a CSDDD audit. Having an ESG report ready gives you a concrete commercial advantage.

esrs.title: The 12 ESRS standards explained
esrs.intro: The European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) are the technical standards that define <3>what to publish. They were adopted in July 2023 and published in the EU Official Journal. There are 12 standards in total: 2 cross-cutting and 10 topical.

esrs1.title: General requirements
esrs1.desc: Reporting principles: double materiality, scope, information quality, report structure. <1>Contains no indicators</1> — it's the methodological framework.

esrs2.title: General disclosures
esrs2.desc: ESG governance, strategy, business model, risk management, stakeholders. ~80 mandatory data points whatever your business.

e1.title: Climate change
e1.desc: Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions (GHG Protocol method), reduction targets, transition plan, physical and transition risks (TCFD-aligned). The most demanding and most audited standard.

e2.title: Pollution
e2.desc: Air emissions (NOx, SOx, particulates), discharges into water and soil, substances of concern (REACH). Mainly relevant for industry.

e3.title: Water and marine resources
e3.desc: Withdrawals, consumption, discharges, water-stress areas (WRI Aqueduct), water efficiency.

e4.title: Biodiversity and ecosystems
e4.desc: Sites located near protected areas, impacts on species, deforestation, MSA (Mean Species Abundance).

e5.title: Resource use and circular economy
e5.desc: Inflows (virgin vs recycled materials), waste generated, reuse rate, eco-design.

s1.title: Own workforce
s1.desc: Demographics (FTEs, contracts, diversity), pay (gender pay gap), working conditions, training, workplace accidents, collective bargaining. ~50 indicators.

s2.title: Value-chain workers
s2.desc: Supplier social audits, coverage rate, human-rights incidents, grievance mechanism. Closely linked to the CSDDD.

s3.title: Affected communities
s3.desc: Impacts on local populations: pollution, expropriation, access to resources. Relevant for industry, extraction, infrastructure.

s4.title: Consumers and end users
s4.desc: Product safety, data protection, accessibility, responsible marketing, complaints.

g1.title: Business conduct
g1.desc: Ethics culture, anti-corruption (incidents, training), supplier-relationship management, lobbying (amounts, topics), whistleblower protection, payment terms.

esrs.note: 💡 You do NOT have to publish all 12 standards in full. Only ESRS 1 and 2 are mandatory in their entirety. For E1-E5, S1-S4 and G1, you apply the principle of double materiality: publishing only the standards deemed material to your business. That is the subject of the next section.

mat.title: The double-materiality analysis
mat.intro: Double materiality is the methodological heart of the CSRD. It's the step that determines which ESRS standards you must publish in detail and which you can set aside or handle quickly.

impact.title: Impact materiality
impact.body: Do your activities have a significant impact on the environment, people or society?
impact.ex: E.g.: a cement plant has a strong climate impact → E1 is material.

financial.title: Financial materiality
financial.body: Do ESG issues affect your financial results (revenue, costs, access to capital, reputation)?
financial.ex: E.g.: an insurer bears climate risk on its portfolio → E1 is material.

mat.orLogic: An issue is material in the CSRD sense as soon as it reaches the materiality threshold on at least one of the two axes (“OR” logic, not “AND”). This is what makes “double” materiality more demanding than the financial-only materiality used by some frameworks (ISSB, for example).
mat.efragTitle: The method recommended by EFRAG (in 5 steps)
mat.step1: Identify the stakeholders, internal and external (employees, customers, suppliers, local residents, NGOs, regulators)
mat.step2: Map the ESG issues of your business (a matrix of ~40-60 issues depending on your sector)
mat.step3: Consult the stakeholders (survey, interviews, workshops) to weight the issues
mat.step4: Assess each issue on both axes (ESG impact × financial impact) on a 1-5 scale
mat.step5: Set the materiality threshold (typically 3/5 on at least one axis) and publish accordingly
mat.exIntro: Imagine a French plastics-processing SME, 180 employees, €35M revenue, located in Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes. Here is a simplified extract of its double-materiality matrix:
mat.exConclusion: This SME would publish E1, E5, S1 and G1 in detail, but treat E2/E3/E4/S2/S3/S4 as “non-material” with a short justification. Result: a 30-40 page report instead of 150.

report.title: The report: structure and technical requirements
report.whereBody: The CSRD report must be published in a dedicated section of the management report (and not a separate document as before the DPEF). In France, the management report is appended to the annual accounts and filed with them at the commercial court registry.
report.formatBody: For listed companies, the report must be published in iXBRL format (Inline eXtensible Business Reporting Language), i.e. an XHTML file that is human-readable <5>and tagged according to the ESRS XBRL taxonomy to allow machine reading (by the AMF, EFRAG, algo investors, etc.).
report.formatNote: For unlisted companies, iXBRL is not mandatory but remains recommended to make the audit easier.
report.auditBody: The report must undergo limited assurance delivered by your statutory auditor or an Independent Third-Party Body (OTI) accredited by COFRAC. It is less demanding than reasonable assurance, but it nonetheless requires:
report.audit1: A documented audit trail for each indicator (source, calculation, validation)
report.audit2: Internal control over ESG data (segregation of duties, hierarchical validation)
report.audit3: Traceability allowing source documents to be traced back in under 24 h
report.auditBoxLabel: 🔒 How ESG Flow helps you pass the audit
report.auditBoxBody: Each report generated in ESG Flow includes a SHA-256 fingerprint of the content, an automatic versioning system and a public endpoint <3>/api/v1/reports/verify that your statutory auditor can query to verify the integrity of a received PDF — useful for your limited-assurance (CSRD) or reasonable-assurance (ISA 3410) work.
report.deadlineBody: The CSRD report is published with the management report, so within 6 months of the financial year-end. For a year ending 31/12, publication by 30/06 of the following year at the latest.

sanctions.title: Sanctions and risks
sanctions.intro: The French legislator (CSRD transposition: ordinance of 6 December 2023) provided several mechanisms to enforce the obligation:
sanctions.s1: Administrative fine from the AMF of up to €3.75M (listed companies) or €50,000 (unlisted) in the event of failure or serious deficiency in publication
sanctions.s2: Statutory-auditor sanctions: refusal to certify, which blocks the approval of the accounts at the general meeting
sanctions.s3: Legal action by NGOs or stakeholders for false or misleading information
sanctions.s4: Exclusion from public tenders with ESG criteria (increasingly common)
sanctions.s5: Reputational risk: the business press is starting to publish the CSRD's “poor performers”
sanctions.boxBody: The real risk for an SME/mid-cap is <1>not the AMF fine (rarely applied to unlisted companies) but exclusion from large-account markets. If you lose a Carrefour, Engie or Bouygues tender because your ESG file is weak, the financial impact far exceeds an administrative fine.

faq.q1: Is my 60-employee company concerned by the CSRD?

faq.q2: What's the difference between the CSRD and the DPEF?

sweep.description: Sweep is a Paris-based carbon accounting and CSRD reporting platform focused on large groups. It has raised $98M and is recognized as an IDC MarketScape Leader 2025.
sweep.pricingNote: No public prices, opaque pricing, many add-ons
sweep.s2: Strong brand recognition on the French market
sweep.verdict: Sweep is excellent for large groups with significant ESG budgets. But with a minimum cost estimated at several thousand euros per month and complex configuration, it is totally unsuited for French SMEs and mid-caps.

workiva.description: Workiva (NYSE: WK) is the global leader in integrated financial + ESG reporting. Listed on the stock exchange, 6,400+ clients, recognized as a Leader by Verdantix, Gartner and IDC. De facto standard for large listed companies.
workiva.s0: Absolute leader in integrated financial + ESG reporting

tsteps.s0Content: This interactive tour (≈ 3 min) walks you through all the platform features. Navigate with Next / Back, skip a step, or relaunch the tour at any time.
tsteps.s1Content: Your real-time ESG cockpit. View your E, S, G scores, trends, priority alerts, and CSRD compliance progress at a glance.
tsteps.s2Content: Record your ESG indicators manually — Scope 1/2/3 emissions, HR social data, governance indicators — through structured forms by pillar.
tsteps.s3Content: Import all your data at once from an Excel or CSV file. The engine automatically detects columns, previews the data, and imports thousands of rows.
tsteps.s4Content: View, filter, and export all your recorded ESG data. Each entry is timestamped, traceable, and linked to its corresponding ESRS indicator.
tsteps.s5Content: Define calculation formulas to automatically derive complex KPIs (e.g. carbon intensity / revenue, adjusted parity ratio) from your raw data.
tsteps.s6Content: Connect your business systems directly: SAP, Workday, Salesforce, SFTP files. Data flows in automatically on the schedule you configure.
tsteps.s7Content: 174 preloaded ESRS indicators (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1). Filter by pillar, instantly see which have data and which are pending.
tsteps.s8Content: Analyse CSRD double materiality: both the financial impact AND the societal impact of your ESG issues. The generated matrix feeds directly into your ESRS report.
tsteps.s9Content: Identify, assess, and prioritise your ESG risks (physical, transition, regulatory). Each risk is linked to action plans and an owner.
tsteps.s10Content: Assess the ESG performance of each supplier, send due-diligence questionnaires, and identify risks in your supply chain.
tsteps.s11Content: Detect anomalies, outliers, and missing data. A global quality score tells you how reliable your reports are before submission.
tsteps.s12Content: Multi-level validation circuit: the contributor enters data, the manager validates, the auditor certifies. Each step is tracked and automatically notified.
tsteps.s13Content: Detailed log of all platform actions with SHA-256 fingerprints. Upload supporting documents, export for your external auditors, and ensure full traceability.
tsteps.s14Content: Automatically calculate your global and per-pillar ESG scores across all your organisations. Identify strengths, weaknesses, and track progress over time.
tsteps.s15Content: Compare your ESG performance with your sector and peers. Position yourself in quartiles and identify best practices to adopt.
tsteps.s16Content: Manage all your entities (subsidiaries, sites, BUs) with their individual ESG score. Native multi-tenant: each organisation has its own data and access rights.
tsteps.s17Content: Artificial intelligence analyses your trends, predicts future scores, and offers personalised recommendations to improve your ESG performance.
tsteps.s18Content: Define your reduction trajectories, create concrete actions by site or BU, and track your progress towards your Net Zero targets in real time.
tsteps.s19Content: Calculate your Scope 1, 2, and 3 carbon footprint using GHG Protocol emission factors. Visualise the breakdown by category and export for your regulatory declaration.
tsteps.s20Content: Assess the alignment of your activities with the European taxonomy (6 environmental objectives). Automatically calculate the percentage of 'green' revenue.
tsteps.s21Content: Track your compliance simultaneously across multiple frameworks: CSRD, GRI, SASB, TCFD, CDP. A unified dashboard for all your regulatory obligations.
tsteps.s22Content: Generate complete CSRD reports in PDF or Word, pre-filled with your data. Schedule automatic exports and share with your auditors in one click.
tsteps.s23Content: Visual CSRD report editor, section by section. Answer ESRS 1 & 2 requirements, add your policies and performance indicators, then export the finalised report.
tsteps.s24Content: Access the ESG Flow REST API Swagger documentation. Integrate your BI tools (Power BI, Tableau) or internal systems via secure webhooks.
tsteps.s25Content: Configure your profile, notification preferences, user access rights, and tenant settings. You're all set — enjoy ESG Flow! 🎉

ptour.s0Content: In 2 minutes, we'll show you how our platform cuts CSRD report production time by 5×, and how our AI turns your ESG risks into a concrete action plan. Ready?
ptour.s1Title: 📊 One Unified View to Steer ESG
ptour.s1Content: Your E, S, G scores in real time, priority alerts, CSRD compliance. Finance, CSR, and Executive teams all share the same dashboard — no more diverging Excel versions.
ptour.s2Content: Smart Excel/CSV import (automatic column detection), or direct integration with SAP, Workday, Salesforce. Your ESG data flows in without manual re-entry — estimated saving: 30 person-days per campaign.
ptour.s3Content: Generate a complete CSRD report, pre-filled with your data and aligned with 10 ESRS standards, in PDF, Word, or XBRL — ready for your statutory auditor.
ptour.s4Content: Our AI analyses your scores, identifies your weak points, and proposes quantified action plans (estimated score gain, effort, deadline). Average score gain: 40% in 12 months among our clients.
ptour.s5Content: Enter your ESG risks and the AI generates a contextualised mitigation plan for each: concrete actions, KPIs to track, deadline. A risk becomes an executable project, not a sticky note.
ptour.s6Content: Book 30 minutes with our team: we set up a demo on your data, your scope, and your sector-specific challenges. Click 'Finish' below to write to us.
